_comment: Inputs for scripts/gen_model.py. Body axes: x forward, y left, z up; origin at the CAD origin (frame centre). Re-run gen_model.py after editing.

frame._source: ROS/EMSD cad/mass_properties.json (QAV-RXL2 CAD; frame, arms, motors, Pi, FC, ESC and wiring)
frame._cad_to_body: The real front is CAD -y, so body = CAD rotated +90 deg about z (confirmed by the team 2026-11-08)

battery._source: Team measurement 2026-11-08 (6S 12000 mAh). Mass to be re-measured; 1.58 kg also quoted.
battery._mount: on top of the frame, long side front to back

motors._source_layout: Motor positions from EMSD drone.json, rotated to body axes. Spin from companion/README.md (verified 2026-10-26). Outputs from FC log 00016 (SERVO1..4_FUNCTION = 36,33,34,35).
motors._source_curve: ROS/EMSD motor_data.xlsx (sheet MQ1053B_6s_StepsTest_thrust_1_r, DShot300, ~24.7 V); fits in sim/README.md
motors._speed_map: rad/s = speed_per_cmd * (cmd + speed_offset), cmd = (PWM-1000)/1000; linear fit of the DC-motor model over cmd 0.15-0.95
motors._max_torque: null = real hardware, no current limit: full output reaches ~2320 rad/s, ~3.8 kgf, ~60 A (extrapolated beyond the bench test's top point of 2.0 kgf / 34.5 A at DShot 1500). The team limits current in firmware with MOT_SPIN_MAX (config/planned_changes.parm). A number here caps motor torque in the model instead (0.289 = 2.0 kgf).
motors._time_constant: assumed (not resolved by the bench test); typical for 8 inch props

payloads.name: water_module
payloads._source: config/payloads/water_module.urdf, from branch manan commit 33f060d (2026-11-15): 20 parts, 482 g, mass properties from STEP normalised to the measured mass.
payloads._mount: Team 2026-11-15: centred under the frame, long side (module y, 197 mm) side to side, so no rotation.
payloads._top_z: Highest point of the CAD in module axes: top of the cap (part 02). ASSUMED to touch the frame's underside; the lid itself is at 29.5 mm, so if the cap fits through a hole in the frame, use 0.0295.
payloads._meshes: From branch manan ROS/watermodule.zip (commit dd3f251) by scripts/import_water_module.py: simplified CAD meshes in module axes. Part names from the STEP products; the CAD only numbers its solids.

visual_meshes._parts: 00 floor + servo brackets, 01 walls, 03 lid: one sealed box

payloads._collision: convex hulls of the tank and of each valve housing; the hanging valves are the lowest point (71.2 mm below the module origin)
payloads._box_size: used only if visual_meshes is removed: solid box with the module's mass and principal inertias

landing_gear._status: ASSUMED, not a real part (2026-11-16). With the water module fitted the drone rests on its two ball valves (~30 mm fore-aft, CoG ~130 mm above them) and tips over, so the sim needs gear to take off and land. Replace with the team's design (open question: leg length and spacing).
landing_gear._legs_xy: 70 % of the motor positions: under the arms, clear of the module (x +-50, y +-99 mm)
landing_gear._bottom_z: 20 mm below the module's lowest point (-118 mm, bottom of the ball valves)

loads.name: water
loads._mass: Team 2026-11-15: up to 500 ml in flight. Override per run: gen_model.py --load water=0 (empty) or =0.25 etc.
loads._tank: Inside of the module's single tank, measured in the CAD meshes (module axes): walls (part 01) at x +-46 and y +-86 mm, floor top (part 00) at z -4.5 mm, lid underside (part 03) at z 24.5 mm. 92 x 172 x 29 mm = 459 ml. The water fills it from the floor up as one rigid block (no sloshing yet). 500 ml does not fit: gen_model.py then fills the tank and warns. The CAD shows no opening between the tank floor and the two ball valves below it, so the valves hold no water here.

aero._comment: Blade-element constants for Gazebo's LiftDrag system; gen_model.py sizes blade area and drag to hit thrust_coeff and torque_coeff.
